Ready to aim high?
Each day, St John’s bursts into life with enthusiasm for what’s to come. Our school community is optimistic, aspirational and determined to squeeze the most out of every opportunity. So, are you ready?

Welcome
In striking surroundings , you will find a creative, ambitious and inclusive community where inquisitive, happy children grow into confident, resilient young adults.
We encourage high standards, both intellectually and emotionally , as we prepare pupils to thrive in a complex world, delivering an outstanding educational experience in the 21st century.
Our much-loved house system and flexible boarding philosophy are our beating heart; fostering fun, friendship and strong relationships that flourish far beyond our walls.
Welcome to St John’s.
Where to?
From the energy of the classroom, to the friendliness of our houses and the buzz of our clubs and societies; St John’s is a school experience like no other.

Work at St John’s
We believe there is no limit to our pupils’ potential and, in this vibrant learning community, we encourage our pupils to work hard, aim high, help others and have fun. None of this is possible without the exceptional team of people who make up St John’s staff. We value the expertise, energy and commitment of our staff across all areas of school life and reward, support and develop our employees accordingly. Attracting and retaining the very best people is fundamental to allowing us to take St John’s forward.
View Current Vacancies
As a co-educational day and flexi-boarding school for over 800 pupils, working at St John’s offers a rich and varied experience for teachers and support staff alike.
Set in the beautiful Surrey countryside, our 50-acre campus is a short stroll into Leatherhead town centre, just 45 minutes by train to the cultural attractions of nearby London, and has excellent transport links by road, rail and nearby airports Heathrow and Gatwick.
We boast a competitive salary structure along with other benefits including a pension scheme, fee reduction for staff children, an employee support and benefits programme, a ride to work and childcare voucher scheme, free lunch during term time, opportunities for professional development and access to sports facilities.

St John's and the Great War
St John’s School, Leatherhead and the Great War, 1914-1919
By Sally Todd and Neil Pudney
Format: Hardback, 160 pages Full colour and fully illustrated Publisher: St John’s School Leatherhead Publication date: 25 November 2019 Dimensions: 280 x 220mm
Price: £25 P&P (UK only) £4.95 per copy
The story told in this book is one of bravery and service, of tragedy and loss. To set the scene, the text begins with a brief history of the School up to 1914, the formation of the Officer Training Corps in 1912, the devastating fire of 1913 and the re-opening of the buildings by the Duchess of Albany on Speech Day, 1 July 1914, just a few weeks before the start of the Great War.
First-hand accounts from OJs who were at school during the war provide a vivid insight into the challenges of daily life of a school in wartime. Food and the lack of it was uppermost in their minds. They describe lessons and learning and the excitement of taking part in or watching the various sports and team games.
In addition to their accounts, we relate tales of wartime heroes, including the two OJs who won the Victoria Cross, families who lost loved ones, and the young men who gave up the prospect of a university education to serve their country, only to be killed in action just a few months or years later.
Many of the stories told here are enhanced by brief biographies giving further background information and celebrating the wide range of accomplishments and achievements of these Old Johnians.
To order a copy, please email the Development Office.

Graduate Sports Assistant (Hockey specialism)
Share job vacancy:
The School is seeking to appoint a graduate with a good degree in any discipline to join our fun, forward-thinking school on a 10-month fixed-term contract
Share job vacancy:
Department
Type
Full Time (in term time)
Closing Date
18 September 2026 9:00 am
Start Date
Fixed Term Contract: End Early July 2027, full-time/term-time only (possibility of further contract extension with PGCE placement)
The School is seeking to appoint a graduate with a good degree in any discipline to join our fun, forward-thinking school on a 10-month fixed-term contract. This is an excellent opportunity to gain valuable experience in an educational setting by contributing fully to the sporting and co-curricular programme at the School. There is also the prospect of getting involved in other aspects of school life for those who are considering a career in teaching and/or wish to take full advantage of the opportunity.
The successful candidate will assist professional sports coaches and PE/games staff across the curriculum. Candidates will be required to have played hockey to a strong club level or above, with coaching experience being highly desirable. A specialism in hockey is essential, and the successful candidate will play an important role in supporting and developing these programmes within the School’s games provision.
The position demands enthusiasm, flexibility, and a positive approach to all games. If you like to work collaboratively and welcome the opportunity to participate fully in a busy and thriving School, we offer a comprehensive induction and CPD programme for all levels of staff, a competitive remuneration package with living out allowance payment, and outstanding, well-equipped facilities. Meals will be provided during term time.
The role is approximately 40 hours per week, term time including inset days. Hours will be worked across 5 days, Monday to Saturday, with the equivalent of one day off per week (to be confirmed on timetable allocation). The role requires flexibility in working hours, including early mornings and evenings. There may be opportunities to be involved in boarding duties; however, any additional hours undertaken in this capacity will fall outside the contracted Sports Graduate hours. The postholder will also be expected to assist with Saturday sports (home and away fixtures) and any other School trips as required.
The placement duration is normally for one academic year, however, subject to academic qualifications of the candidate, the academic requirements of the School, and completion of the PGCE application process, there may be the possibility to extend for a further year, with PGCE placement support for 2027/2028.
Closing Date: 9.00am, Friday 18 September 2026
Interviews will be held w/c 21 September 2026
Interviews may occur at any stage after applications are received. We reserve the right to appoint at any time in the recruitment process and therefore invite interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.
Full details can be downloaded below
Candidate Brief – Graduate Sport Assistant- Hockey Sept 2026
Application for Employment – Support Staff
Equal Opportunities Monitoring Form

St John’s School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people, and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. Applicants must be willing to undergo child protection screening appropriate to the post, including checks with past employers and the Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS).
The job holder should be aware of their responsibilities for promoting and safeguarding the welfare of children and young persons who they may come into contact with whilst at St John’s adhere to and ensuring compliance with the School’s Child Protection Policy Statement at all times.
The post is exempt from the Rehabilitation of Offenders Act 1974 and the School is therefore permitted to ask job applicants to declare all convictions and cautions (including those which are “spent” unless they are “protected” under the DBS filtering rules) in order to assess their suitability to work with children.”

Performing Arts
Our Performing Arts Department is an energetic, creative and inclusive hub that strives to promote committed, passionate and diverse performances in music, drama and dance. We have one central goal: to encourage and foster a true love and enjoyment of performing for all. We are proud of our imaginative provision and programming, always striving to get the best out of our pupils through a diverse and busy schedule of performances across all year groups.
Music
Music is a vibrant and inclusive part of life at St John’s, where pupils of all ages, abilities and interests are encouraged to perform, create and develop as musicians. From choirs, orchestras and bands to competitions, masterclasses and major concerts, there are opportunities for everyone to get involved and flourish. Our pupils explore an eclectic range of genres and enjoy incredible opportunities, including performing with professional orchestras and taking to renowned stages, including Cadogan Hall in London and St Peter's Basilica in the Vatican.
Drama
Drama at St John’s is of the highest standard, developing true commitment and dedication from pupils and staff alike. From major musicals and plays to cabarets, film projects and backstage roles, pupils explore a wide range of theatrical styles while developing teamwork, creativity and communication skills. Drama is also available at GCSE and A Level. Supported by outstanding facilities and expert teaching, drama fosters artistic expression and unforgettable experiences for performers and production crews alike.
Dance
Dance has grown hugely in popularity over the last few years, fuelled in part by the department’s reputation for musical theatre and with our cohort of dance teachers, and we are happy to present the opportunity for pupils to engage in tap, hip-hop, jazz and musical theatre clubs across lunchtimes and activities while also having the opportunity to engage in peripatetic one-to-one dance lessons. From September 2026, pupils will be able to study Dance at GCSE.
Events
Throughout the St John's year there are dozens of Performing Arts events, from lunchtime recitals, drama and music workshops and interhouse competitions to the Concerto Competition, the Forbes Music Competition and the St John's Musical at Leatherhead Theatre.
Performing Arts Scholars
We offer both overarching Performing Arts Scholarships as well as dedicated Music Scholarships for Year 7, Year 9 and Sixth Form entrants, as well as individual Drama Scholarships for Sixth Form only. Alongside numerous performance opportunities, scholars benefit from personalised mentoring and guidance, exclusive masterclasses with industry professionals, and creative leadership opportunities, with many scholars going on to study at elite institutions after leaving St John's.
2025-2026 Statistics
Performing Arts Facilities
As a School we are fortunate to enjoy excellently equipped performance spaces. Facilities include our purpose-built Performing Arts Centre auditorium, complete with excellent sound and lighting equipment, and the beautifully restored Old Chapel and Chapel, each housing meticulously maintained Yamaha grand pianos. The Performing Arts Centre is also home to a vast array of intimate performance spaces, peripatetic teaching and practice rooms, two drama spaces, two highly equipped music suites and a recording studio.

Careers and Futures
At St John’s we believe that it is essential to prepare pupils for the future, and that this is about far more than just qualifications. We encourage our pupils to be conscious of what we call the ‘formula for success’: Success = Qualifications + Skills + Experience + Contacts. To ensure they can succeed in whichever path they choose, we want to help our pupils understand the job market and what it is that employers may be looking for, and to build impressive profiles to make them stand out in a competitive world.
We know that the job market is dynamic and constantly evolving, therefore we want to facilitate our pupils to be confident, skilled, experienced individuals who can thrive in the future, whatever it may hold.
Careers education begins in Lower School during enrichment lessons, where pupils are introduced to the multitudes of career paths available and the skills that employers are looking for, as well as reflecting on the changing nature of the job market. Upper Third pupils include research and reflections on careers in their personal projects to help them consider how their own interests relate to the working world.
In the Fourth Form, pupils are given support and advice as they make their GCSE choices, with both pupils and parents having the option to arrange one-to-one meetings with the Head of Careers to discuss the options they are considering. The Fourth Form also take part in a Careers Carousel, where they experience workshops in a wide range of careers such as medicine, law, finance, marketing and property, to encourage them to begin thinking about what working in such industries might involve.
In their GCSE years, we facilitate and encourage pupils to take ownership of the research and decision-making for their futures. They are given access to Unifrog, a platform which allows them to complete personal profiling, research subjects, careers, apprenticeships and much more, as well as to record their skills and achievements and start building a CV. Parents also have access to this platform to support their children. GCSE pupils also join the St John’s Careers Team network, where numerous competitions, work experience placements and other opportunities are advertised, and they are actively encouraged to take part in these.
Upper Fifth pupils attend the A level Options Evening and have personalised one-to-one conversations with their tutors to guide them on choosing their A levels. They are actively encouraged to meet with the Head of Careers and/or the Head of Sixth Form if they need further guidance.
Sixth Form pupils are encouraged to continue to use the Careers Team network and Unifrog, particularly for university research and to write their personal statements, and these are widely utilised. Sixth Form pupils are expected to complete work experience, which they record on Unifrog, and we support them in finding their placement.
Pupils are given the opportunity to attend various talks on different pathways, such as degree apprenticeships and applying to American universities, and to hear from students who are currently following such pathways; St John’s pupils who are considering these pathways receive personalised support from the Head of Careers throughout the process.
Lower Sixth pupils take part in Core Curriculum lessons to develop their skills and understanding on topics which will be essential for their futures, such as financial literacy, political understanding and professional presentation, and these core curriculum lessons often give them the opportunity to hear from inspiring speakers from different professions. Visiting career and industry experts also run workshops on Enrichment Days, for example interview skills and CV writing. Sixth Form pupils take part in several university visits, including Sussex University and the University of Oxford, to get a sense of what university life involves, as well as receiving in-school talks from university representatives from universities such as Warwick and Bath.
Those applying to Oxford or Cambridge have one-to-one progress meetings with subject specialists and the Head of Sixth Form Enrichment to produce, develop and revise their personalised action plans, and also take part in a mock interview with external subject specialists. Those who are required to complete admissions tests such as the LNAT or TSA are given preparation classes for these towards the end of the Lower Sixth to ensure they are fully prepared. Specific societies exist for popular careers, such as law, medicine and psychology, to ensure that pupils who are interested in these careers have the opportunity to develop their knowledge and understanding. Towards the end of the Lower Sixth and in the Upper Sixth, pupils are given extensive guidance on their personal statements and university applications, including a Personal Statement Day and dedicated tutor time.
We hold an annual Careers Convention in October, where St John’s pupils and parents have the opportunity to meet, converse and network with approximately 50-60 representatives from a wide range of different fields. Pupils in the Fifth and Sixth Forms also have the opportunity to sign up for a wide range of careers talks and workshops with representatives from different careers which occur over the course of the year. Examples of recent workshops include: business skills with Unilever, media, clinical psychology, medicine and criminal law. We encourage pupils to seek individual support with anything related to their future, and thrice-weekly careers lunchtime drop-in sessions are available for all pupils if they would like to discuss anything with the Head of Careers, or pupils are welcome to make an appointment at another time.
We produce a bi-annual careers newsletter, Future Focus, to celebrate everything pupils are doing to prepare for the future, and to discuss pertinent careers and university related issues.

Celebrating 175 Years of St John's
Creative Arts
Artistic life flourishes at St John’s. Our pupils seize the opportunity to explore their imaginations, try out new techniques, find outlets for their self-expression, and enjoy being creative.
Stunning art works adorn the walls as you walk around the School and our dedicated art studios are inspiring places, where artists have scope to experiment under the guidance and tutelage of our talented and passionate staff.
As pupils learn about art, work in different media, visit exhibitions and develop their own ability and style, their horizons are broadened and they become of aware of the many ways in which art enriches all our lives.
Sixth Form Art
Art A level at St John’s encourages students to develop their creative voice through experimental thinking, technical skill, and independent exploration. With access to excellent studio facilities and specialist guidance, pupils are able to investigate a wide range of media and concepts. The course nurtures confidence, originality, and a strong portfolio that supports progression into creative higher education and careers.
Regular updates from the St John’s art department can be found on their dedicated Instagram account.

Our People
Our dedicated, enthusiastic and talented staff embody St John's mission to create an environment that is kind, supportive and full of opportunity, that inspires and equips pupils to thrive now and in the future. Here are a few key people you will meet when you visit St John's.
Alex Tate MA(Oxon)
Alex Tate MA(Oxon)
As The Head of St John’s, Alex has responsibility for the overall vision, ethos and strategic leadership of the School.
Alex became The Head of St John’s School in 2023.
Alex Mogford MA
Alex Mogford MA
Alex was appointed Senior Deputy Head in September 2024, having previously held the roles of Deputy Head (Pastoral) and Assistant Head (Head of Sixth Form) at St John’s.
The Senior Deputy Head has overall responsibility for the operational and strategic delivery of the academic and pastoral life of the School.
Harrie Todd BA
Chief Operating Officer
Harrie Todd BA
Chief Operating Officer
Harrie was appointed Chief Operating Officer (COO) in June 2024.
The COO has overall responsibility for the operational and strategic delivery of support functions of the school including Finance, Estates, Operations, HR and IT.
Leah Hilt BSW
Director of Safeguarding
Leah Hilt BSW
Director of Safeguarding
Leah took up the post of Director of Safeguarding in June 2022, following a successful career in Children’s Social Care within both Canada and the UK.
Leah leads safeguarding across the school, enabling the school’s safeguarding provision to be delivered effectively at both strategic and operational levels. She holds the primary Designated Safeguarding Lead role and supports the Deputy Designated Safeguarding Team.
Ian White BSc MA
Deputy Head (Co-curricular and Logistics)
Ian White BSc MA
Deputy Head (Co-curricular and Logistics)
Ian was appointed Deputy Head (Co-Curricular and Logistics) in September 2022, having previously held the roles of Assistant Head (Upper School), Housemaster and Head of Department.
The Deputy Head (Co-Curricular and Logistics) has overall responsibility for the operational and strategic delivery of the Co-Curricular programme as well as responsibility for whole school logistical and operational matters relating to pupil experiences.
Richard Harvey BA
Assistant Head (Safeguarding)
Richard Harvey BA
Assistant Head (Safeguarding)
Having previously served as Head of Lower School, Richard now leads and oversees the School’s safeguarding prrovision, ensuring that the welfare, safety and wellbeing of pupils remain at the heart of school life.
Andy Bass BEd
Assistant Head (Upper School)
Andy Bass BEd
Assistant Head (Upper School)
In his role as Assistant Head (Upper School), Andy oversees the important transition into the Fourth Form. He tracks and supports the academic progress of all pupils from the Fourth Form to the Upper Fifth, guiding both GCSE and A level choices.
Liz Pritchett PhD MEd BA
Assistant Head (Pastoral Care)
Liz Pritchett PhD MEd BA
Assistant Head (Pastoral Care)
Liz was appointed Assistant Head (Pastoral Care) since 2024 and was previously the Housemistress of Haslewood.
In her role as Assistant Head (Pastoral Care), Liz oversees individual pastoral care for all pupils at St John’s and works with Senior House Staff to coordinate broader pastoral strategy and oversee tutoring provision across the School.
Hannah Rowell BSc
Assistant Head (Lower School)
Hannah Rowell BSc
Assistant Head (Lower School)
In her role as Head of Lower School, Hannah oversees all aspects of life in the Lower School, from making sure our youngest pupils swiftly settle in when they join Lower Third to developing academic and co-curricular enrichment opportunities. Hannah previously served as Housemistress of Gloucester.
Rosalind Williams BA
Assistant Head (Sixth Form)
Rosalind Williams BA
Assistant Head (Sixth Form)
As Assistant Head (Sixth Form), Ros oversees all aspects of life in the Sixth Form at St John’s, ensuring pupils get the most out of these two important years of their school life from studying for A levels and enjoying a rich co-curricular programme to making well-informed choices about their future.
Craig Holland BSc
Craig Holland BSc
As Director of Sport, Craig is responsible for developing an innovative sports programme which gives St John’s pupils access to the highest standards of coaching, equipping them with the ability to live active, healthy lives and enabling them to fulfil their sporting potential, as well as running a busy programme of competitive fixtures.
Oliver White BA PGDip RCM FISM
Director of Performing Arts
Oliver White BA PGDip RCM FISM
Director of Performing Arts
Ollie leads a passionate and energetic Performing Arts Department, encouraging and inspiring pupils to contribute to performance through music, drama and dance and creating a busy, enjoyable calendar of events which adds colour and vibrancy to life at St John’s.

Register Online
We welcome applicants to register for entry to the School for Lower Third (11+ Year 7) 2027, Fourth Form (13+ Year 9) 2029 and Lower Sixth (16+ Year 12) 2027 and beyond. Closing date for registration is 1 November 2026 of Year Six for Lower Third and Fourth Form applicants, and 15 October of Year 11 for Sixth Form applicants. For more information, visit our Admissions Process and Admissions FAQs pages.
The registration fee of £220 is payable by all applicants, unless they are eligible for Free School Meals. Please contact Admissions with proof of eligibility before completing the registration form.
For overseas applicants the fee is £320. Overseas applicants should complete the registration form below, and pay the fee of £220. Once this is complete, please email Admissions to arrange the appropriate bank transfer of the remaining £100.
Applicants looking for occasional places should contact Admissions.
When completing the registration form you need to have popups enabled on your device as it relies on a popup when the payment method is chosen. Payments will show on credit card statements as Iris Payments.
To contact Admissions, please email: admissions@stjohns.surrey.sch.uk

The St John’s Community
The sense of community at St John’s is something of which we are exceptionally proud. We're an open, welcoming school which encourages its pupils to look beyond their immediate surroundings to be aware of their role in – and their ability to contribute to – the wider community.
Current Parents
Current parents play an active and important role in school life, through the St John’s Parent Association (SJPA) and through their dedication, enthusiasm and support for a huge variety of school events. From supporting on the sidelines at sports fixtures, to cheering on the latest performing arts productions, we love welcoming parents into school. It says a lot about the deep-rooted sense of community that many parents maintain links with St John’s even after their children have left the School. They enrich school life in countless ways and we are grateful for everything they do.
Old Johnians
Our alumni - the OJs - is an active and enthusiastic group which offers opportunities for networking, careers advice, friendship and a host of enjoyable activities. We love hearing from, and meeting up with, our former pupils and greatly value the lifelong connections so many of them maintain with St John's.
Our Wider Community
We're fortunate to have extensive links with local groups, other schools and organisations. We appreciate the opportunities we can offer to others and the benefits that those relationships bring to the richness of St John’s life. From Duke of Edinburgh's Award volunteering and helping in local schools, to inviting primary aged pupils to St John's for lessons or sports training, and organising our annual Community Holiday, we are proud of the variety of ways in which our pupils contribute to society.
Development
We are passionate about widening access to St John's and creating life-changing opportunities for young people. We want to open doors and unlock potential so that as many promising children as possible, regardless of their background or ability to pay fees, are able to benefit from everything that a St John’s education offers. Founded to provide a free education to some of the poorest members of society, St John's has - with the generous help of our donors - provided this support ever since. It is central to our ethos and an important part of what we do.

Our History
St John’s 175
This year, we’re proud to mark an incredible milestone – 175 years of St John’s School. Throughout this anniversary year, we will reflect on our remarkable history and look ahead with confidence, supported with a fantastic programme of events planned to honour our heritage and future vision.
St John's History
Founded in 1851 by clergyman Ashby Haslewood, St John’s began as a school to provide free education for the sons of poor clergymen. Over the 20th and 21st centuries, we have evolved to become a thriving fully co-educational day and boarding school for approaching 900 pupils. Today, the School continues to build on its legacy – providing a rounded education that equips our pupils with emotional intelligence, flexibility, and resilience to thrive in an ever-changing world.
Below you’ll find all the information about events taking place at St John’s during our 175th anniversary year. There is more to come, so watch this space!
What's Happening This Year
The Quad Life Skills Curriculum Launch – September 2026
Since its foundation, St John’s has prided itself on providing an all-round education, recognising that while exam results and qualifications matter, they sit alongside skills such as leadership, proactivity, critical thinking, and ethical problem solving. With the world today very different than the one St John’s was founded in, we are taking a major step forward in our curriculum design with the launch of the Quad Life Skills programme in September 2026. For more information, visit our Life Skills page.
Heritage Day – 12 September 2026
To mark the 175th anniversary of the School, we are expanding our highly sought Heritage Open Day offering on 12 September, providing members of the St John’s community and the wider public with a chance to explore the School’s history. Tours are available at 10.00am, 11.00am, 12.00pm, and 2.00pm. Tickets can be booked here. For more information, visit our Heritage Open Day page.
OJ Dinner – 2 October 2026
The OJ Dinner will take place on 2 October 2026, and all OJs are invited to attend to celebrate the schools 175th anniversary with a drinks reception and 3-course meal.
Windsor Evensong – 7 October 2026
Heading off site, St John’s choirs are heading to the historic St George’s Chapel, Windsor, to perform a choral evensong. Part of Windsor Castle, and the site of royal weddings, burials and other services for more than 500 years, St George’s is one of the most iconic and historically significant venues in the country, and will provide a truly magical space for St John’s pupils to perform in.
Remembrance – 8 November 2026
Our Remembrance Service on Sunday 8 November is open to all the St John’s community – pupils, parents, family, friends, staff and OJs – as we remember the many St John’s pupils who gave their lives in service to the country.
Nine Lessons and Carols – 14 December 2026
All are welcome to our traditional Nine Lessons and Carols service in the St John’s Chapel on 14 December. With Christmas anthems performed by the School Choir and Schola Cantorum, this is a wonderful festive way to bring the school year to an end.
"Big School" Opens – January 2027
One of the oldest parts of the St John’s building was historically known as “Big School” – a large building that served as assembly hall, dining room, gymnasium and much more for the School’s early pupils. Since then it has served a variety of roles under a number of different names, but in January 2027 it will re-open as “Big School” once again… providing a new, renovated space for our Sixth Form pupils, including a café, lecture space, study centre and offices for our Sixth Form staff.
OJ Festival – 26 June 2027
To round off our 175 year, we’re delighted to be hosting an OJ Festival, combining an alumni sports tournament with other celebratory events throughout the summer afternoon. More details to follow!
Stay up to date with all our 175 events by visiting the Forthcoming Events page. You can also catch up on St John's news by clicking the Latest News link below.
